subject: Customer report: sustained latency + 503s — quota window/burst suspected
body:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@covehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@covehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & 503s across QA and Prod

Hi Rafael —

We started seeing sustained high latencies around 08:50 PT this morning and a growing number of 503s. Our SRE dashboard shows 95th percentile generation latency up from ~350ms to 2.1s and error spikes coinciding with peak batch jobs. This is impacting two of our customer-facing features (clinical-summary generation).

Sample errors: 2026-06-09T08:57:12Z 503 /v1/generate token-bucket-rejected, 2026-06-09T09:04:21Z 503 downstream timeout.

Can you escalate and confirm whether this is on your side (rate limiting / quota) or something we need to change client-side? We have an executive review at 2pm PT and need a short status.

Attaching a screenshot of our SRE graphs (latency_screenshot.png).

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Director of Engineering — CoveHealth

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@covehealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@covehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & 503s across QA and Prod

Rafael / Monica / CoveHealth —

Preliminary triage from infra: we see correlated 503s that map to token-bucket rejections in our rate limiter. The policy applied to the CoveHealth API key had a very small burst window (burst_tokens=50, window_ms=100), causing the KV cache + batching patterns from your recent client-side tuning to exhaust the burst quickly during short traffic spikes. When the bucket depletes, requests fall back to fast-fail (503) rather than queue, which explains the sudden spikes in error rate and the longer tail seen in latency when requests do get through.

What I ran: sampled request traces and the rate-limiter counters (attached snapshot). We also found an older policy override that was supposed to be environment-scoped but got applied to the prod key in the policy merge step (likely a config mistake during a recent rollout).

Proposed immediate mitigations (1–2 hour impact window):
- Apply temporary override to increase burst_tokens to 120 and window_ms to 1000 for the CoveHealth prod key (reduces quick rejections).
- Enable conservative queuing (short queue depth) as a fallback for 30 minutes while we monitor.
- Roll back the misapplied policy from the policy-merge layer.

We can push the override now if CoveHealth approves. This is a config-level fix; no code change required. I'll attach the policy snapshot and logs for your review.

Attachments: quota_policy_snapshot_raf-4831.json

-Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

---
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@covehealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@covehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & 503s across QA and Prod

Elena / Samir —

Thanks Karthik, and thanks for the clear plan. CoveHealth — Karthik is recommending a short, temporary policy override that should stop the 503s and reduce the latency tail while we roll back the incorrect merge. We can schedule the override to be applied immediately and monitor for 60–90 minutes.

Before we proceed: can you confirm peak sustained QPS during the incident window and whether you expect any large batch jobs to continue in the next hour? If you want, we can apply the override for just the next 60 minutes and then revert while we finish the policy rollback.

I'll also attach our collected logs to help with your postmortem.

Attachments: support_logs_2026-06-09.zip

Thanks,
Rafael

Rafael —

Confirmed. Peak sustained QPS during the incident was ~380 rps for a 6-minute window. We have an analytics job scheduled at 12:30 PT but can pause it if needed. Please proceed with the temporary override now; we approve the 60-minute window.

—Samir
SRE Manager — CoveHealth

Subject: Exec brief request — CoveHealth incident

Rafael / Monica —

Thanks for handling the CoveHealth incident. Quick ask: I need a short exec brief for the customer call and our leadership sync tomorrow morning. Please include:
- Impact summary (minutes of service degradation, estimated affected requests)
- Root cause synopsis (policy merge + burst window misconfiguration)
- Actions taken (override, rollback, monitoring) and timelines
- Customer asks and proposed commercial gesture (recommend up to 10% credit for the affected billing period)

Rafael: please draft a 1‑pager we can share externally — Monica can finalize the wording. Karthik: can you confirm the exact config keys that were misapplied so we can add the remediation checklist?

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
